newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends little changed after fluctuation.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends little changed after fluctuation.

text.p: The won closed little changed after a fluctuation following what dealers said was an intervention by the central bank to support the local currency.
The won closed at 843.40, compared with the day's opening rate of 843.30. It ranged from 842.70 to 844.30.
Dealers said the won was trading at 843.90 in the afternoon when the Bank of Korea was seen heavily selling dollars, pushing up the won to an intraday high of 842.70.
Bank of Korea officials were not available to comment.
Dealers estimated the central bank's dollar selling at about $100 million.
They said the won's sudden rise was quickly followed by dollar buying by traders who thought the won would remain weak for the time being in line with a slump in exports.
"It's highly likely the 845 won level will remain a ceiling for the dollar for the rest of this year," said a dealer.
Dealers said the won's base mid-rate was expected to be pegged at 843.70 on Thursday, compared with Wednesday's 843.10.
